Bail Bond Information for Bexar County

After booking into Bexar County jail, a judge typically sets bail at arraignment (often within 24–72 hours). Families often work with a licensed bail bondsman. A common commercial bond fee is about 10% of the bail amount (non-refundable). Example: $10,000 bail → roughly $1,000 premium, subject to local rules.

If the person cannot afford bail, they may request a reduction hearing or public defender.

For hearing schedules, contact the Bexar County court.

What to Expect After Arrest in Bexar County

Typical steps after arrest in Bexar County:

  1. Booking — fingerprints, photo, property inventory
  2. Medical screening — before general population housing
  3. Classification — housing based on charges and history
  4. Arraignment — first court appearance; bail often set here

Frequently Asked Questions — Bexar County Inmate Lookup

How do I find out if someone is in Bexar County jail?

Start with the official Bexar County inmate roster. You can also call Bexar County Sheriff's Office at (210) 335-6201. Online records often lag booking by a few hours.

What is the phone number for Bexar County Adult Detention Center?

Contact Bexar County Sheriff's Office at (210) 335-6201. Facility address on file: 200 N Comal St, San Antonio, TX 78207.

How long does booking take in Bexar County?

Booking commonly takes 2–8 hours depending on volume at Bexar County Adult Detention Center. Weekends and holidays can delay when a name appears in any published system. If urgent, call the facility directly rather than waiting on a website refresh.

Can I visit an inmate at Bexar County jail?

Usually yes if the person is eligible and the facility is accepting visits. The main facility listed is Bexar County Adult Detention Center at 200 N Comal St, San Antonio, TX 78207. Bring government photo ID and confirm hours and dress code with Bexar County Sheriff's Office before you go. Video visitation may be offered.

What if the person is not listed in the county system?

They may have been released, transferred, or booked under a different name spelling. Check Texas Department of Corrections and the Federal BOP locator for federal custody. Then call Bexar County Sheriff's Office to confirm.

How do I send money to someone at Bexar County Adult Detention Center?

Ask Bexar County Adult Detention Center which commissary vendor they use (often JPay, Securus, or Access Corrections) when you call (210) 335-6201. Limits and fees vary by facility — confirm before sending money.
